chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Among the wisdoms of the progeny of Dawud (peace be upon him) is that the intellectual should be aware of his time, attentive to his affairs, and preserving his tongue.
ai.seo_question: What are the essential characteristics of an intellectual according to the wisdom of the progeny of Dawud?
ai.summary: Attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in al-Kafi, this narration defines the 'wisdom of the family of Dawud' as a triad of temporal awareness, focused diligence, and linguistic restraint. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *hilm* (forbearance) and *hifz al-lisan* (guarding the tongue) as essential markers of the *'aqil* (discerning one), linking intellectual maturity to social prudence. This tradition serves as a practical guide for navigating societal complexities while maintaining spiritual integrity.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Usman Bin Isa, from Saeed Bin Yasaar, from Mansour Bin Yunus, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘In the wisdom of the progeny of Dawood<sup>as</sup>, it is upon the intellectual that he become the most understanding one of his time period, attentive upon his occupation, preserving of his tongue’.
en.sarwar: 20. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kufi from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sa’id ibn Yasar from Mansur ibn Yunus from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“It is in the wisdom of Ale (people of) Dawud: ‘A person of reason must learn about the nature of his time, pay attention to his affairs and safeguard his tongue.’”
